description: Main window. Files (workbench-design/sandboxing-plan.md, phase 3): the window reads $APPDATA and $RESOURCE, writes $APPDATA only, and reaches anything else only through a native dialog pick — the dialog plugin adds each pick to the fs plugin's runtime scope, which tauri-plugin-persisted-scope keeps across restarts in $APPDATA/.persisted-scope. A pick is readable and writable (a library folder must be both); a folder that is read deeply is picked with recursive: true. Each fs command is granted on its own, with its own scope, and no fs permission SET is used: fs:default and fs:allow-appdata-*-recursive bring in $RESOURCE and the other app folders, which would leave the installed app writable. src-tauri/src/capability_tests.rs sends real fs calls through the IPC against this file to prove it. Write commands (write-text-file, rename, remove, open — open takes write options from the window) reach $APPDATA/** only; on Unix that glob never matches a dotfile, so Rust's own records (.approved-programs.json, .persisted-scope) can be neither written nor removed, and mkdir alone may name $APPDATA itself, to create it. A pick could still name a record (a save dialog aimed at it, one click on Save), so the fs:scope deny on $APPDATA/.* refuses Rust's dotfiles to every command whatever was picked: denies are checked before any allow, the runtime scope's included. read and seek act on a file the window has already opened, so they carry no scope. Programs (pandoc, Diogenes' perl exporter, the AI CLIs) run only through the app's own job commands in src-tauri/src/commands.rs, which take no program path or argv from the window; app commands need no capability entry beyond core:default. core:window:allow-destroy is what the close button needs (src/App.svelte: save every editor, then destroy). opener:allow-reveal-item-in-dir is 'Reveal in Finder' after an export.
